title: GEAR: From Dynamic Encoding to Dynamic Activation in Social Trajectory Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2609.13778v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Human trajectory prediction requires modeling both individual motion patterns and social interactions among agents. Existing methods have made substantial progress by using attention mechanisms, graph structures, and temporal encoders to capture dynamic social context. However, most of them primarily focus on how social information is encoded, while paying less explicit attention to how the encoded social context should take effect during future trajectory generation. In this paper, we argue that dynamic social encoding does not necessarily imply dynamic social activation. The same interaction context may require different activation strengths across future horizons and scene densities: social cues should be strengthened when interaction evidence is strong, but suppressed when they are weak or noisy. translated_title: GEAR：从动态编码到动态激活的社会轨迹预测
translated_abstract: 人类轨迹预测需要对个体运动模式以及智能体之间的社会交互进行建模。现有方法通过注意力机制、图结构和时间编码器来捕捉动态社会背景，已取得了显著进展。然而，这些方法大多主要关注社会信息如何被编码，而较少明确关注编码后的社会背景应如何在生成未来轨迹的过程中发挥作用。在本文中，我们提出：动态的社会编码并不必然意味着动态的社会激活。相同的交互上下文在不同的未来时间范围和场景密度下可能需要不同的激活强度：当交互证据较强时应加强社会线索，而当社会线索微弱或含噪声时应予以抑制。为解决这一问题，我们提出了GEAR，一种面向人类轨迹预测的生成感知偏置激活模型。该模型建立在偏置分解……
tldr: 提出GEAR模型，通过生成感知的偏置激活机制，使编码后的社会线索在轨迹生成过程中根据交互证据的强度进行动态强化或抑制，从而提升人类轨迹预测的效果。
en_tdlr: GEAR introduces a generation-aware bias activation mechanism that dynamically strengthens or suppresses encoded social cues during trajectory generation based on the strength of interaction evidence, improving human trajectory prediction.
